messages:
Alex: quick heads-up — noticed a big quota spike this morning tied to ephemeral service accounts on project-juice.
Mira: ugh, saw that alert too. Is it a burst of legit traffic or a credential reuse loop?
Sam: logs look like repeated short-lived token minting every ~30s from the same job runner.
Jess: can you paste a sample? might be the k8s sidecar renewing too often.
Alex: here are the relevant lines from token-service:
```
INFO 2026-03-20 09:12:01 mint token sa:ephemeral-237 for project:juice ttl:60s
INFO 2026-03-20 09:12:31 mint token sa:ephemeral-237 for project:juice ttl:60s
INFO 2026-03-20 09:13:01 mint token sa:ephemeral-237 for project:juice ttl:60s
```
Priya: that pattern will blow past project quota because attribution currently maps to the service account's org owner, not the originating project's pipeline.
Mira: right — the console dashboards show the org as the hot actor, which confuses owners and triggers org-level alarms.
Sam: two problems: (1) attribution granularity and (2) quota circuit-breaker treats ephemeral SA as a single actor so fallback throttles org-wide.
Jess: proposal: include an `origin_project` claim in ephemeral tokens at mint time and have the quota router inspect it for attribution/routing.
Alex: +1, but we need to think about trust: who can set `origin_project`? it must be asserted by the mint service, not callers.
Priya: exactly. token-service should populate `origin_project` from the authenticated caller context. clients cannot supply it.
Mira: and on the console side we should surface both org- and project-level time-series for ephemeral token usage, with a toggle in the rollouts UX.
Sam: ops question: will routing by `origin_project` affect fallback policies? e.g., can we route to cheaper capacity when project is low-cost tier?
Jess: yes — routing policy already supports an `attributes` bag. We can add `origin_project` to that bag and use rules for quota/route decisions.
Alex: test plan: (1) token-service adds claim + telemetry; (2) quota router reads claim; (3) console adds attribution line item; (4) gradual rollout with feature flag.
Priya: +1. For telemetry, also emit `ephemeral_sa.signature` + sample of `mint_count` per minute to avoid noisy cardinality.
Mira: can we do a canary deploy for the router change? want to avoid misattributing traffic mid-quota-window.
Sam: deploy-bot started canary `quota-router/v2` to 10% in prod :eyes:
deploy-bot: canary deploy quota-router/v2 -> 10% across us-west clusters. Monitor `quota.drop_rate` and `attribution.mismatch`.
Jess: I'll wire an alert on `attribution.mismatch > 1%` for 5m and mute org-level paging during the canary to avoid noise.
Alex: thanks — assigning Priya + Sam to implement token claim and router read. Mira + Jess for console + alerts. I'll own the rollout doc.
Priya: started a draft PR: https://git.internal/redwood/token-service/pulls/402 — adds origin_project claim and telemetry.
Mira: noted. let's sync tomorrow 10am to verify dashboards post-canary.
Alex: ok, closing loop here. thanks all :thumbsup:
